prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1068; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for side impact collision at intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a vehicle that ran a red signal. Police report requested. Initial contact made with claimant by phone. Claimant reports being treated at the scene and later discharged from urgent care with a concussion diagnosis. Claimant is not represented by counsel.

Entry 2: Recorded claimant's statement by phone. Claimant describes headaches, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating since the collision. Claimant has not yet returned to work. Advised claimant of the right to seek legal advice and of the process for medical documentation. Requested authorization to obtain treatment records.

Entry 3: Received police report. Citing officer notes the other driver admitted to not seeing the signal. Witness statement on file corroborates claimant's account that the claimant had a green light. Liability appears clear in favor of claimant, pending review of signal timing data from the city.

Entry 4: Obtained medical records from urgent care. Diagnosis confirmed as mild concussion with recommendation for follow-up with a neurologist. Claimant has scheduled a follow-up appointment. Bodily injury evaluation placed on hold until treatment progress is documented. Reminded claimant to keep all receipts for out-of-pocket medical expenses.

Entry 5: Spoke with claimant regarding follow-up care. Claimant reports symptoms are improving slowly but remain present. Reviewed the claims process again and confirmed claimant may contact the adjuster directly with questions. Diary set for thirty days to review updated medical records and reassess injury component.
